description: Player 1's deck for the Sheepish spec. Two cards carry the scenario and both cost one mana, so a single two-mana turn holds the whole sequence. #11 Tempo Timmy is the Unit whose play springs the trap: it has no Cry, so nothing about the transform can be confused with a Cry that fizzled, and - the reason it is Tempo Timmy and not #8 Mr. Vanilla - it is not Immutable, which R17 and R23 would let refuse the Transform outright ("Sheepish on an Immutable unit still fires and is consumed with no effect"). #15 Me and Mr Token is the Unit played immediately afterwards: its Cry summons a Rush Token, so the token on the board is the proof that player 1 could continue and that the next play's Cry still fires (R118). The other eighteen are choice-free filler that keeps the deck legal and never opens a picker; nothing here is a Trap, a Cast-on-draw card or a Quickdraw card, so the only trap in the game is player 2's. No card here carries a start-of-turn, end-of-turn or on-play hook that acts on the board (#58 Rush Token Farm and #64 Gifted Program were removed for exactly that): `triggerHoldersWithHook` in packages/engine/src/triggers.ts gathers those hooks from the HAND as well as the field, so a Rush Token Farm sitting in hand summons a unit every turn and a Gifted Program in hand makes a cheap play Radiant - which would move the board and the stats this spec asserts. Reported as an engine finding; the fixture does not rely on it either way.
